_rules: 0) 保留 ** 强调、`code`、链接与表格结构，与中文侧逐块对应。
1) 官方英文引文原样保留；档案里的中文转述引文在英文侧标注 (translated)，不伪造英文原文。
2) 「未核验/官方未给」等未知语义不升级；不借翻译改事实。

axes.model_access: **The official readable pages (docs intro and release notes) show no "user picks the model" surface** — models and versions are decided on the vendor side. This is common to the vendor-cloud form (this site's judgement, based on "checked the intro page, no model-selection docs found" — not on "the official states selection is unavailable").
axes.runtime: **Sessions run in Devin's cloud workspace**: the web app (app.devin.ai) embeds a three-piece set — Shell (watch commands execute), an embedded IDE (take over and edit code live), and a Browser (watch it read docs / test the app). There is also **Devin for Terminal** (installed from cli.devin.ai) running on your machine, with `/handoff` sending long tasks to the cloud Devin; plus the Devin API.
axes.local_files: Cloud sessions do not touch your local files — it clones, edits and opens PRs on repositories you authorize; repo visibility is set by integration grants. **The Terminal form is the exception**: it runs directly in your local environment, taking over the local codebase.
axes.background: **The main axis is asynchrony**: the official defines it as an "autonomous AI software engineer", suited to handling multiple tasks in parallel — Linear/Jira issues, whole new features, bug reproduction and fixes, migrations and refactors. The official rule of thumb (original wording): "if you can do it in three hours, Devin can most likely do it" (tasks with high verifiability have higher success rates).
axes.tools: The workspace ships with three tool classes — shell, browser, IDE. Dispatch tasks by @Devin directly in Slack/Teams threads; Linear/Jira issue-line integrations exist. **MCP support status: not verified one by one** (docs have an integrations section; not read page by page this pass).
axes.context: Work is organized per session; the knowledge-accumulation/memory surface is not verified one by one. The official recommends writing tasks with clear completion criteria, broken into verifiable steps — how much context to give is decided when you dispatch.
axes.permissions: Account + organization system: enterprise admins assign permissions; repository access is scoped by integration grants (GitHub etc.); API access is configured separately. The cloud environment has internet access (the Browser tool is part of the product semantics) — the official asks you to treat it by the standard you would apply to a public compute surface.
axes.fit:
Good fit: delegating backlogged issues in bulk, running multiple tasks in parallel, @-dispatching casually in Slack, wanting "a draft PR first, then take over".

Not a fit: wanting model choice, wanting fully local execution end to end (Terminal only covers light tasks), keeping secrets inside the cloned repositories.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (three, each pointing at something the official readable pages do not give):

- **Whether a model-choice surface actually exists** — no model-selection page found in the official docs; logging in and measuring can confirm
- **End-to-end latency and failure-retry behavior from Slack dispatch to PR opened**
- **How uncommitted local changes are handled during Terminal ↔ /handoff transitions**
unknowns:
- Whether a model-choice surface exists (not found in official docs; not measured)
- MCP support status (docs integrations section not read page by page)
- Details of the knowledge/memory accumulation mechanism (not verified one by one)
- Details of the cloud workspace's network egress and persistence policy (not verified one by one)
